correctness.rationale: I rechecked the complete repaired RESULT.md and SLOGAN.txt in /workspace/repairs/1/. Scalar opposite-sign returns satisfy a memory consistency relation ruling out unequal magnitudes; each crossed coordinate contributes zero or ±(h/2−ε/a) and the global sign quotient gives the credited census, with no additional coordinate option at equality. The active half-return block has determinant β and trace s=−1+3β+2(1−β)/q, q=ha/(2ε)>1; conjugation by the sign flip gives its square as the return derivative. The three strict Schur inequalities hold on 3β−1<s<1+β. At zero the relative derivative follows from the O(|x|√v⁺) error term, so the frozen text's 'every cycle' smoothness description is corrected: only all-active cycles have strictly positive memory in all coordinates. The repaired proof supplies the two zero-coordinate multipliers, a local expansion/contraction argument in the actual state space, and the product count of 2^(k−1) attracting cycles off threshold equalities. At their positive-memory states the implicit function argument persists under small symmetric Hessian perturbations. The determinant lower bound is attained exactly at |s|≤2√β; monotone s(q) gives the stated q_− and q_+ (finite upper edge only when β<1/9). The intersection of the rescaled bands is precisely the inclusive curvature cutoff; if empty, the spectral radius stays strictly above β even at the infimum by its endpoint limits and continuity. Replay: python /workspace/checks/1.py (SymPy symbolic Jacobian and exact samples). At β=1/16 it gives endpoints 10/7 and 6, ratio 21/5; a mixed cycle with h=3, ε=1 and curvatures 1 and 3/5 has radius 16/25 even though its nonzero block is on the plateau. Frozen verify.py and its output were read, not executed. The spectral optimum concerns all-active cycles, not critical boundary stability, a mixed-orbit global optimum, or a uniform pure-power norm estimate.

value.rationale: The repair isolates the exact attractor count at all noncritical stepsizes and the sharp attainable local linear rate for the diagonal family. The coupled condition-number bound gives an actionable distinction between an individual block's optimal rate and joint attainability at a single stepsize. This remains useful beyond known existence and near-threshold stability, without counting the prior orbit census as an independent contribution or implying global attraction.
